name: Dörvöljin District
terrain: The Great Lakes Depression is an endorheic basin in western Mongolia with lake deposits and old shorelines.
analogRationale: Proposed because it falls in a very dry rainfall class and is remote, and a search found no analog study of it. Published Mars analog work on Mongolian lakes concerns the Gobi-Altai transition zone and the Valley of the Gobi Lakes, not this basin.

name: Taklamakan Desert
terrain: The Taklamakan is a dune desert that is normally dry in winter because of the surrounding mountains.
analogRationale: A 2019 JpGU conference abstract measured perchlorate in Taklimakan samples and proposed the desert as a Mars analog, and a 2007 microbial study of Chinese deserts by NASA Ames researchers included a site along its southern edge. Neither source places the work at this exact point in Makit County.

name: Dasht-e Kavir

name: Harrat Ash Shaam
terrain: Large volcanic field on the Arabian Plate with more than 800 cones and basaltic lava flows.
analogRationale: Proposed because it is a young basaltic volcanic field in a dry, remote setting. A search found no analog study at this point in Jordan. A 2019 LPSC abstract treats the "jubot" depressions on the field's northwest margin as analogs for Martian pit craters, which is a Mars comparison rather than a lunar one.

The published comparison is to Mars rather than the Moon, so this place is listed under Mars.
